chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from al-Faḍl Abī al-ʿAbbās, who said:

“If moisture from a dog reaches your garment, then wash it; and if it touched it while dry, then pour water over it.” I said: “Why has it come to hold this status?” He said: “Because the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered that they be killed.”

key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog, whose contact is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَنْزِلَةِ: status or legal standing in this context
key_terms.رُطُوبَةٌ: moisture or wetness transferred by contact
key_terms.فَاصْبُبْ عَلَيْهِ الْمَاءَ: then pour water over it, indicating the prescribed purification action
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it, indicating cleansing by washing

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a dog touches one's clothing according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a garment contacted by a dog, distinguishing between wet and dry contact. It also cites a Prophetic basis for the dog's legal status in this context, presenting the ruling within the framework of ritual purity.
